clue.text: Retiring from transport company surprisingly flush

parts.note: BA is British Airways

indicators.note: the letters of flush turn up in an unexpected order

parts.note: taken as written

explanation.surface: Someone flush with cash takes early retirement from a transport firm.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Retiring' looks like leaving work, but it means shy; 'flush' is not wealthy but the fodder.
explanation.definitionFit: A retiring person is shy and reserved, a straightforward synonym.

clue.text: Bend sinister at the bottom in shield

parts.note: to buckle is to bend under pressure

indicators.note: in a down clue the bottom of the word is its last letter

parts.note: the last letter of sinister

explanation.surface: A heraldic bend sinister appears at the base of a shield.
explanation.walkthrough: A bend sinister is a diagonal band on a coat of arms, so the surface is all heraldry while the parse breaks it apart.
explanation.definitionFit: A buckler is a small round shield held by a handle.

clue.text: Peter amended tiny part of Bible giving reason to stick together

parts.note: peter is old criminal slang for a safe, as in a safecracker's peterman

indicators.note: the letters of tiny are corrected into a new order

parts.note: taken as written
Numbers is the fourth book of the Old Testament

explanation.surface: Someone named Peter edits a small section of scripture to argue for unity.
explanation.walkthrough: Peter suggests the apostle, given the Bible nearby, but it is thieves' slang for a safe.
explanation.definitionFit: Safety in numbers is the idea that a group is more protected than an individual, a reason to stay together.

clue.text: Charges current politician over void lease for land ownership

parts.note: fees are charges for a service
I is the physics symbol for electric current
MP, Member of Parliament

indicators.note: emptied of its middle, so only the outer letters of lease remain

parts.note: first and last letters of lease

explanation.surface: A politician levies charges on an empty lease.
explanation.walkthrough: In a down clue 'over' just places one piece above the next.
explanation.definitionFit: Fee simple is the legal term for absolute freehold title to land.

clue.text: Smashed bulb may be so

definitions.meaning: first meaning: drunk, slang for intoxicated
second meaning: a light bulb that is switched on and glowing

explanation.walkthrough: 'Smashed bulb' reads as broken glass, but the two halves are separate meanings.
explanation.definitionFit: The phrase is slang for drunk and also describes something illuminated.

clue.text: Skilful concealing old British firm's shortfall

indicators.note: the word for skilful hides the firm inside itself

parts.note: deft means skilful with the hands
ICI was Imperial Chemical Industries, a former British industrial giant

explanation.surface: A clever accountant hides a former British company's losses.
explanation.walkthrough: ICI was a major British chemicals company, broken up in 2008.
explanation.definitionFit: A deficit is the amount by which money falls short of what is needed.

clue.text: Grilled cheese scoffed after case of Drambuie

indicators.note: the cheese and scoffed pieces follow the Drambuie letters
the case is the outside, so only the first and last letters of Drambuie

parts.note: first and last letters of Drambuie, a Scotch whisky liqueur
Brie is a soft French cheese
fed means ate, as in fed on

explanation.surface: Cheese on toast is wolfed down after a case of whisky liqueur.
explanation.walkthrough: Drambuie is a Scotch whisky liqueur; 'Grilled' suggests cheese on toast but means questioned.
explanation.definitionFit: To debrief someone is to question them closely after a mission, i.e. to interrogate.

clue.text: Official admitting hesitation over having more autonomy

indicators.note: in a down clue the whole thing is turned over, reading upwards
the referee lets the hesitation in

parts.note: a ref is a referee, a match official
er is the sound of hesitating

explanation.surface: A referee hesitates over whether to give a player more freedom.
explanation.definitionFit: Freer is the comparative of free, so less constrained and more independent.

clue.text: Succeeded cracking puzzles needing brains and hard fight

indicators.note: the succeeded abbreviation breaks into the middle of the puzzles word

parts.note: crosswords are word puzzles
S is the genealogical abbreviation for succeeded
wit is intelligence

explanation.surface: Solving puzzles takes intelligence and a hard struggle.
explanation.walkthrough: The S goes in after CROSS, splitting the puzzles into the swords of a duel.
explanation.definitionFit: To cross swords with someone is to argue or clash with them, an idiom for fighting.

clue.text: In front of uncovered king, captures rooks

indicators.note: the captures word comes before the king piece

parts.note: takes as in chess captures

indicators.note: with its outer letters stripped off, leaving only the middle of king

parts.note: king without its first and last letters

explanation.surface: A chess move: with the king exposed, a piece captures the rooks.
explanation.walkthrough: 'rooks' reads as chess pieces but is the verb meaning swindles.
explanation.definitionFit: To take someone in, like to rook them, is to cheat or deceive them.

clue.text: Conspicuous volume of doubly fine drugs swallowed by company board with caution

indicators.note: the doubled letters and drugs go down inside the company-and-board pieces, as food is swallowed

parts.note: a table is a board, as in bed and board

indicators.note: says the letter for fine appears two times over in the string

parts.note: F is the abbreviation for fine, as on pencil leads
E is ecstasy, so drugs in the plural gives two of them
to book a player is to caution them

explanation.surface: A company's board is cautioned over drug taking, all written up in a showy volume.
explanation.walkthrough: 'swallowed by' works on company and board read together, so the doubled fine letter and the drugs sit between those two words' letters; 'drugs' is plural, so ecstasy's E comes twice.
explanation.definitionFit: A coffee-table book is a large showy illustrated volume meant to be displayed rather than read, so conspicuous is its point.

clue.text: Not entirely cool at hip club in India

indicators.note: only part of the phrase cool at hip is used, the run of letters spanning its words

parts.note: the letters run across these words, ending inside hip

explanation.surface: Someone hip at an Indian club is not entirely cool.
explanation.walkthrough: A lathi is a heavy bamboo stick carried by Indian police.
explanation.definitionFit: A lathi is a long weighted stick used as a weapon in South Asia, i.e. a kind of cudgel.

clue.text: Puritan and saint drinking wine — they may be in bed

indicators.note: the puritan and saint pair take the wine inside them

parts.note: prim describes a prudish, puritanical person
rosé is pink wine

explanation.surface: A puritan and a saint are drinking wine, and then end up in bed together.
explanation.walkthrough: The bed is a flower bed, not a bedroom one.
explanation.definitionFit: Primroses are pale yellow spring flowers commonly planted in garden borders.

clue.text: Setter dons apron for cooking, keeping dry

indicators.note: to don clothing is to put it on, so the jumbled apron letters wrap around the setter
the letters of apron for are being worked into a new mix

parts.note: taken as written
taken as written
the crossword setter refers to themself as I

explanation.surface: The setter puts on an apron before getting down to cooking.
explanation.walkthrough: 'for' looks like a link word but its letters are part of the mix.
explanation.definitionFit: Something rainproof resists water, so it keeps whatever it covers from getting wet.

clue.text: Start travelling to Nigeria

indicators.note: the letters of to Nigeria move about into a new order

parts.note: taken as written
taken as written

explanation.surface: A journey to Nigeria begins.
explanation.definitionFit: To originate is to begin or come into being.

clue.text: Statesperson, one given bagel and pasty

parts.note: I is the Roman numeral for one
a bagel is ring-shaped, like the letter O
a pasty complexion is pale, or wan

explanation.surface: A politician is handed a bagel and a pasty for lunch.
explanation.walkthrough: 'pasty' looks like a pie (a Cornish pasty) but is the adjective meaning pale.
explanation.definitionFit: An Iowan is a native of Iowa, so a person from one of the US states.

clue.text: Trendy blackguard has debts with no interest

parts.note: in means fashionable
a cur is a contemptible man
IOUs are written acknowledgements of debt

explanation.surface: A fashionable scoundrel runs up debts without paying any interest.
explanation.walkthrough: 'no interest' suggests a loan, but it means lack of curiosity.
explanation.definitionFit: Someone incurious lacks curiosity and shows no desire to find things out.

clue.text: 4x4 car, not Rover or Sierra

indicators.note: the car's name is taken without the word Rover

parts.note: the Range Rover is a British four-wheel-drive vehicle
taken as written

explanation.surface: A buyer wants a four-wheel drive, but neither a Rover nor a Ford Sierra.
explanation.walkthrough: The Sierra was a Ford family car, so the surface reads as a list of models; here it is the Spanish-derived word for mountains.
explanation.definitionFit: A sierra is a chain of mountains with a jagged outline, i.e. a mountain range.

clue.text: Spinner, which is unaffected by spinning?

indicators.note: turning the word end to end leaves it exactly the same, so it reads identically either way

parts.note: the spinner itself, whose name is the thing tested

explanation.surface: A riddle about a spinning thing that stays the same when spun.
explanation.walkthrough: The definition and the wordplay share the idea of spinning.
explanation.definitionFit: A rotator is something that rotates, as a muscle or device turning on an axis.

clue.text: Being crude, oil's kept here without saving the planet?

indicators.note: used in the old sense of outside, so the drum phrase goes around the green piece

parts.note: oil is stored in a drum, so the place is in drum
eco- is the prefix for environmentally friendly things

explanation.surface: Crude oil is stockpiled somewhere with no thought for the environment.
explanation.walkthrough: 'crude' suggests oil, but here it means vulgar; 'without' means outside.
explanation.definitionFit: Indecorum is improper or unseemly behaviour, which is what being crude amounts to.

clue.text: Inappropriately, give hands to married ladies when dancing

indicators.note: the letters of ladies jig about into a new order

parts.note: taken as written

explanation.surface: At a dance, married women are inappropriately handed partners.
explanation.walkthrough: The hands are hands of cards.
explanation.definitionFit: To misdeal is to distribute cards wrongly among the players.

clue.text: Stall worker given zero extra cash

parts.note: a temp is a temporary office worker
O looks like zero
a rise is a pay increase

explanation.surface: A worker at a market stall gets no pay rise at all.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Stall' looks like a market stall but is the verb meaning to delay.
explanation.definitionFit: To temporise is to delay or play for time to avoid committing oneself.

clue.text: Female leaving old seafood

indicators.note: the female abbreviation departs from the word for old

parts.note: former means old, as in a former president

explanation.surface: A woman walks away from some stale seafood.
explanation.walkthrough: An ormer is an abalone, a shellfish prized in the Channel Islands.
explanation.definitionFit: The ormer is an edible sea snail, a type of shellfish eaten as a delicacy.

clue.text: Finish eg trifle, extremely nice after turnover

indicators.note: the whole is turned over, which in a down clue sends it upwards

parts.note: trifle is an example of a pud, British slang for pudding

indicators.note: only the extreme letters of nice, its first and last

parts.note: first and last letters of nice

explanation.surface: A meal ends with trifle, which is very nice after an apple turnover.
explanation.walkthrough: A turnover is also a pastry, and trifle is a British layered dessert of sponge, custard and cream.
explanation.definitionFit: To end up is to finish in a particular place or state.

clue.text: Game's involving two bridge players getting tricks

indicators.note: the game's letters enclose the two players

parts.note: RU is rugby union, with the S of the possessive
South and East are two of the four bridge positions

explanation.surface: A card game in which two bridge partners take tricks.
explanation.walkthrough: 'tricks' looks like the bridge term, but it means deceptions.
explanation.definitionFit: Ruses are cunning schemes intended to deceive, so tricks in the con-artist sense.

clue.text: Film version of Hamlet with antic Dane trapping foreign king

indicators.note: a new version reworks the letters of the play's title

parts.note: taken as written

indicators.note: the jumbled Dane letters hold the king inside them
antic means grotesque or capering, so the letters of Dane are jumbled

parts.note: taken as written
Louis was the name of many French kings

explanation.surface: A film adaptation of Hamlet in which the mad Dane imprisons a foreign monarch.
explanation.walkthrough: Hamlet feigns an 'antic disposition', so 'antic Dane' reads as the prince himself.
explanation.definitionFit: Thelma & Louise is Ridley Scott's 1991 road movie starring Geena Davis and Susan Sarandon.

clue.text: What tennis player does after a let shows modesty

definitions.text: What tennis player does after a let
definitions.meaning: first meaning: after a let the point is replayed, so the player serves again
second meaning: reticence, holding oneself back

explanation.walkthrough: Read the first part as RE-SERVE, serving once more.
explanation.definitionFit: Reserve as a personality trait is restraint and reticence, close to modesty.

clue.text: Philosopher astride horse or kind of lamb

indicators.note: the philosopher's name sits over the horse, one part either side

parts.note: Blaise Pascal, the French philosopher and mathematician
H is slang for heroin, itself called horse

explanation.surface: A philosopher sits on a horse, or perhaps a lamb.
explanation.walkthrough: Horse is drug slang for heroin, whose abbreviation is H.
explanation.definitionFit: The Paschal lamb is the lamb sacrificed at Passover, the adjective meaning of Passover or Easter.
